criteria.name: Fees
criteria.description: Advisory fee and low-balance fee drag at $5,000

options.name: Betterment
options.summary: 0.25% or flat monthly fee at low balances, TLH at all balances, near-zero minimum

options.name: Schwab Intelligent Portfolios
options.summary: No advisory fee but cash drag; TLH only from $50,000

scores.rationale: Daily TLH claimed, low-reliability source; direct indexing minimum disputed
0.25% but flat monthly fee at low balances is high effective rate
No advisory fee but cash drag size disputed

recommendation.headline: Wealthfront: flat 0.25% fee and tax-loss harvesting for a $5,000 account
recommendation.summary: Wealthfront combines a flat 0.25% fee with tax-loss harvesting and clears its $500 minimum easily; Betterment is a close second.

tradeoffs.text: Direct indexing minimum disputed; Wealthfront TLH cadence from a low-reliability source

alternatives.when: Want goal-based tools or very small starting balance; check whether the flat monthly fee applies
Already a Schwab customer and tax-loss harvesting is irrelevant (IRA)
Want a bigger brokerage ecosystem at 0.30%

caveats: Fees and minimums change; confirm on provider sites
nextSteps: Confirm Wealthfront TLH eligibility on its site

contradictions.assessment: Source 6 says $5,000, sources 2,4,5 say $100K, source 3 says $500K; majority and consistent figure is $100K. Not relevant to a $5,000 decision.
NerdWallet (source 1, reliability 82) lists it with automated TLH; source 2 (48, undated) says no. Source 1 more credible.
Source 2 says 6-10%, source 4 says 6-30%; both agree on a mandatory cash drag.

uncertainties.text: Wealthfront daily TLH relies on low-reliability source 2
Betterment low-balance fee threshold and how to waive it differ across sources
NerdWallet's Wealthfront TLH minimum text was truncated
